These fixtures are partly verified. The D8 probe (2026-11-05, zellij 0.45.1, private socket dir, panes running /bin/sh,
/bin/cat, /bin/sleep and a byte recorder) printed the shapes below; ids, paths, session names and the pane commands
are placeholders. The probe log is ~/.paseo/reports/sidekick-ultra/reviews/d8-probe-zellij.log.

Verified by the probe:
  list_panes_*.json        `zellij --session S action list-panes --all --json --command --state` -> a JSON array of
                           panes with id, is_plugin, is_focused, exited, exit_status, is_held, title, tab_id, tab_name,
                           terminal_command, plugin_url, ... A terminal pane adds pane_command ("/bin/sh",
                           "/bin/sleep 300": the running command line) and pane_cwd. There is no pid. Plugin panes
                           (is_plugin true) share ids with terminal panes: plugin 0 and terminal 0 coexist.
  new_pane.txt             `new-pane --direction right --no-focus ...` prints "terminal_N" and leaves focus alone.
  `write-chars --pane-id terminal_N -- TEXT`
                           no Enter, LF stays LF, a leading "-" is safe after "--". To a missing pane it exits 0 and
                           drops the text, which is why send checks the pane first.
  `send-keys --pane-id terminal_N Enter`, `focus-pane-id terminal_N`
                           worked as the backend uses them.
  A missing session        exit 1 with "Session '...' not found".
  `list-sessions -n -s`    printed one session name per line (list_sessions.txt) while a session existed.

Settled by the live run at 24c6bd1 (~/.paseo/reports/sidekick-ultra/reviews/d8-zellij-24c6bd1.log, outside phase):
  `list-sessions -n -s` with no session
                           exit 1, empty stdout, stderr "No active zellij sessions found." The backend's guess matches.
  pane_command argv0 of a stub started as `exec -a claude /bin/bash stub` (bash stub, new-pane with an absolute path)
                           "claude" and "codex": discovery, attach and the argv0 match worked. The stubs are now
                           `exec -a <name> /bin/dd`; the next live run must show that argv0 again.
  `write-chars` to a missing pane
                           exit 0 (reproduced), so the send guard is needed.
  send, focus, the gone-pane guard, the not_in_mux refusal
                           all passed. "submit presses Enter" failed because the old stub could not record a CR
                           (bash `read` turns CR into LF); the new stub records raw bytes with dd.

Still unverified (the live run, tests/live/zellij.sh, must settle each):
  `new-pane` that prints no id
                           at 24c6bd1 (inside start) and at 58637a7 (setup) a `new-pane --direction right` exited 0 with
                           empty stdout. Both were the 4th right split of a headless session 50 columns wide. Reading
                           zellij v0.45.1 (zellij-server/src/tab/mod.rs): with no room to split, zellij closes the
                           freshly spawned pane and returns Ok, so no pane exists and no id is printed; with floating
                           panes visible, or a floating target pane, it returns early with nothing created. The server
                           also waits only 1 s for the pane (route.rs), so a slow server could print nothing for a
                           pane it did create. The backend's error says all of this. The live script now keeps nvim's
                           tab roomy (stubs in other tabs), and records one deliberate no-room split in a scratch tab:
                           exit, stdout, stderr first line, pane counts before and after, and the tab's panes.
  pane_command for a tool started with env
                           start puts "/usr/bin/env K=V claude" in front of the tool. Whether pane_command then shows
                           "env" or the exec'd tool, and for how long, is unknown. The backend records the tool's
                           command name as proc_name when argv0 is still "env", and is_running asks the tool's is_proc,
                           so the session counts as running once env has exec'd the tool. While the pane still shows
                           "env" (or the stub's bash), is_running is false. The live script observes the state at once
                           and gates on running within 3 s.
  pane_command of a tool typed into a shell pane
                           every stub runs as the pane's own command. Whether pane_command shows the shell or its
                           foreground child when a tool is typed into /bin/sh is not known. The live script types the
                           stub into a /bin/sh pane and records the argv0 and whether discovery found it (an
                           observation, not a gate).
  pane_command of a held pane
                           the exited fixture (terminal_3) has exited true and no pane_command, as the probe saw for an
                           exited pane. Whether a pane held after its command ended reports the same is not known; the
                           backend skips any pane with exited true.
  list-panes on an exited (resurrectable) session
                           `list-sessions -s` may name it. The backend skips a session whose list-panes fails with
                           "Session '...' not found" (exit 1) and reports every other failure.
  focus-pane-id for a pane in another tab
                           the probe and the live run used one tab. Whether focus-pane-id switches tabs is not known
                           (design 11 left "go-to-tab-by-id first" open).
  tools installed as scripts
                           a tool installed as `#!/usr/bin/env node` may show argv0 "node" and go undiscovered. Not
                           tested; the same family as the rex argv0 match.
